prompt: Some people feel that manufacturers and supermarkets have the responsibility to reduce the amount of packaging of goods. Others argue that customers should avoid buying goods with a lot of packaging. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
It is often argued that manufacturers and supermarkets should reduce the amount of packaging used for goods, while others believe that customers should avoid purchasing heavily packaged products. Both views have some valid points. However, I personally believe that businesses should bear greater responsibility because they control packaging decisions and can reduce waste on a much larger scale.

On the one hand, I believe that manufacturers and supermarkets should take greater responsibility for reducing excessive packaging. One important reason is that they control how products are packed and presented to consumers. If businesses remove unnecessary materials and replace them with recyclable alternatives, the amount of waste can be reduced at its source. For instance, a large supermarket could replace excessive plastic wrapping with recyclable paper. This would reduce plastic waste and environmental pollution. Furthermore, large manufacturers usually have the financial and technical resources to develop more sustainable packaging. By introducing recyclable materials across thousands of products, they can create a much larger environmental benefit than individual consumers can achieve.

On the other hand, some people argue that customers should avoid buying products with excessive packaging. Their purchasing decisions can influence businesses because companies usually respond to changes in consumer demand. When shoppers consistently choose products with minimal or recyclable packaging, supermarkets may offer more environmentally friendly alternatives. For example, if customers regularly choose products with simple recyclable packaging, a supermarket may increase its supply of such goods. As a result, consumer behaviour can contribute to wider changes in the market. Nevertheless, customers cannot directly control how products are designed and packaged. Although responsible purchasing is useful, it should complement rather than replace the responsibility of manufacturers and supermarkets.

In conclusion, although customers can encourage businesses to reduce packaging through their purchasing choices, I believe that manufacturers and supermarkets should bear the greater responsibility. They have direct control over packaging decisions and can reduce environmental waste on a much larger scale.
